# graph-io conformance report

Every fixture is imported as bytes and compared with an expectation taken from an independent
reader or the format's specification. A known failure is a case where graph-io does not meet
the expectation today; the reference points into
`sources.md` next to this report (the research notes behind this corpus).

| csv | 83 | 69 | 14 | 67 | 1 |

## networkx differential

`tools/differential.py` writes seeded networkx graphs with networkx 3.1's own writers into
`fixtures/<format>/networkx-generated/` and records networkx's read-back as the expectation;
they are counted in the table above. Where networkx departs from the specification the
expectation follows the specification and the entry says why.

| Format | Files | Conform | Known failures | networkx overruled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| csv | 24 | 24 | 0 | 0 |
| gexf | 30 | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| gml | 30 | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| graphml | 60 | 60 | 0 | 8 |
| json | 60 | 38 | 22 | 30 |
| pajek | 30 | 30 | 0 | 0 |

Where networkx is overruled:

- graphml: networkx writes multigraph edge keys as GraphML edge ids, which repeat across node pairs; GraphML requires edge ids unique within the document, so networkx's read-back (every edge kept) is not the expectation: graph-io reports E_DUPLICATE_EDGE_ID for each repeat (8 files)
- json: networkx keys its read-back nodes by data.value and writes edge ends as the original Python keys, while Cytoscape.js ids are the data.id strings (Cytoscape.js turns a numeric id, source or target into its string); the top-level `directed` key is a networkx extension the elements JSON does not define, so direction is not asserted (30 files)

## Generative round trips

fast-check graphs (seed 20260923, 300 per configuration; generative.ts) are
exported, re-imported from bytes and compared with the original. A difference is allowed only
when a check() note announced it (the table below); an export that throws only when check()
announced an E_ code (a documented refusal).

| Configuration | Graphs | Equal | Documented refusals | Skipped (known failure) | Documented losses exercised |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gexf | 300 | 289 | 11 (E_XML_ILLEGAL_CHAR) | 0 | idText |
| gexf 1.2 | 300 | 289 | 11 (E_XML_ILLEGAL_CHAR) | 0 | idText |
| graphml | 300 | 289 | 11 (E_XML_ILLEGAL_CHAR) | 0 | idText |
| gml | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | boolAsInt |
| dot | 300 | 268 | 32 (E_DOT_TRAILING_BACKSLASH) | 0 | idText, negativeZero, nonFiniteText, textInferred |
| pajek | 300 | 115 | 133 (E_PAJEK_TEXT) | 52 | idText, negativeZero, nonFiniteText, textInferred |
| csv | 300 | 274 | 0 | 26 | direction, idText, negativeZero, nodeOrder, nonFiniteText, textInferred |
| neo4j | 300 | 218 | 0 | 82 | direction, idText |
| json node-link | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | negativeZero, nonFiniteUnset |
| json jgf | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | idString, negativeZero, nodeOrder, nonFiniteUnset |
| json cytoscape | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | direction, negativeZero, nonFiniteUnset |
| json graphology | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | negativeZero, nonFiniteUnset |

The documented losses (a check() note code and the difference it allows):

- `W_ID_TEXT_TYPE`: idText
- `W_NUMERIC_IDS_STRINGIFIED`: idString
- `W_NODE_ORDER`: nodeOrder
- `W_CSV_NODE_ORDER`: nodeOrder
- `W_DIRECTION_DROPPED`: direction
- `W_CSV_DIRECTION_DROPPED`: direction
- `W_NEO4J_UNDIRECTED_AS_DIRECTED`: direction
- `W_NONFINITE_AS_NULL`: nonFiniteUnset
- `W_DOT_NON_FINITE`: nonFiniteText, textInferred
- `W_PAJEK_NONFINITE_AS_TEXT`: nonFiniteText, textInferred
- `W_CSV_NONFINITE`: nonFiniteText, textInferred
- `W_TEXT_INFERRED`: textInferred, negativeZero
- `W_DTYPE_UNSUPPORTED`: boolAsInt
- `W_INTEGRAL_F64_AS_I32`: negativeZero

Minimal cases (`fixtures/generative/cases.json`):

- `negative-zero-weight` (12 configuration(s)): an explicit weight of -0 keeps its sign (was written as 0 by every weight formatter). fixed, regression
- `negative-zero-cell` (8 configuration(s)): an f64 cell of -0 next to a non-integral value keeps its sign (formatF64 and the JSON writer wrote 0). fixed, regression
- `lone-negative-zero-column` (3 configuration(s)): an f64 column holding only -0 is written -0.0 and must be widened to f64 on reading (the text writer believed the sink inferred f64 for -0; graph-format infers i32). fixed, regression
- `json-integral-after-nonfinite` (4 configuration(s)): an f64 column of [-0, NaN]: NaN is written as null, so the column reads back i32; check() must announce W_INTEGRAL_F64_AS_I32. fixed, regression
- `dot-backslash-newline` (1 configuration(s)): a text holding a backslash before a line break is a Graphviz line continuation; export() must refuse it (E_DOT_TRAILING_BACKSLASH) rather than write a text that reads back without both characters. fixed, regression
- `csv-edgeless-undirected` (1 configuration(s)): an undirected graph without edges has no Type cell to carry its direction; check() must announce W_CSV_DIRECTION_DROPPED. fixed, regression
- `pajek-numeric-text-parameter` (1 configuration(s)): a string parameter holding -3 reads back as a number; check() must announce W_TEXT_INFERRED. fixed, regression
- `pajek-infinite-weight` (1 configuration(s)): an infinite edge weight. known failure: pajek: an infinite edge weight is written as `Infinity`, which the Pajek importer reads as a parameter name without a value (E_PAJEK_LINE) and drops the edge; check() announces nothing. Pajek has no spelling for infinity: check() should refuse or note it
- `csv-one-column-node-table-pipe` (1 configuration(s)): a node table with the Id column only, an id holding `|`. known failure: csv: a one-column node table is written with a bare `|`, `;` or tab inside an id, and the importer's delimiter sniff picks that character, splitting the rows (E_CSV_FIELD_COUNT). The exporter should quote a cell holding any sniffable delimiter when the table has one column
- `gml-list-marker-text` (1 configuration(s)): a text cell holding "[]". known failure: gml: a text cell equal to NetworkX's list markers ("[]", "()", "_networkx_list_start") is written as that string and read back as a list; check() announces nothing. Either note it (the NetworkX convention makes the text ambiguous) or write such a text so it cannot be taken for a marker
- `neo4j-tab-in-quoted-id` (1 configuration(s)): an id holding tabs, on a node with three self-loops. known failure: neo4j: the importer sniffs the delimiter; the one-column :ID section gives no evidence for the comma, the quoted ids' tabs repeat evenly, so the file is read tab-delimited and every relationship row fails (text after a closing quote). neo4j-admin uses a comma unless told otherwise

Graphs the properties skip until the known failure is fixed:

- pajek: an infinite edge weight is written as `Infinity`, which the Pajek importer reads as a parameter name without a value (E_PAJEK_LINE) and drops the edge; check() announces nothing
- csv: a one-column node table (ids only) is written with a bare `|`, `;` or tab in an id, and the importer's delimiter sniff picks that character, splitting the rows (E_CSV_FIELD_COUNT)
- gml: a text cell equal to NetworkX's list markers ("[]", "()", "_networkx_list_start") is written as that string and read back as a list; check() announces nothing
- neo4j: the importer sniffs the delimiter: a file whose first section has one column and whose quoted cells hold tabs is read tab-delimited, and the comma-delimited rows fail (text after a closing quote); neo4j-admin's delimiter is a comma unless told otherwise

## Schema validation

Validated 934 dot, 961 gexf-1.2draft, 962 gexf-1.3, 962 graphml, 972 jgf exports (GraphML 1.0 XSD, GEXF 1.2draft and 1.3 XSDs, JGF v2 JSON Schema; schemas.ts);
420 documents have at least one error.

| Class | Errors | Kind | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| GEXF viz namespace (gexf) | 179 | deviation | the XSDs are generated by trang from the normative RNC, whose `default namespace = inherit` puts color / position / size / shape in the GEXF namespace; the gexf.net samples, the primer, Gephi and networkx all write them in the viz namespace, and so does graph-io |
| GraphML nested-graph keyref (graphml) | 205 | deviation | node_id_key selects .//node in EVERY graph, so a nested graph's keys reach its parent's table twice and libxml2 rejects an outer edge into a nested graph; the GraphML primer's own nested.graphml fails identically |
| NMTOKEN character edition (graphml) | 327 | deviation | libxml2 checks xs:NMTOKEN with the XML 1.0 second-edition character classes (XSD 1.0); graph-io's NMTOKEN test uses the XML 1.0 fifth-edition name characters (supplementary planes, U+FFFD...), which XSD 1.1 processors and every non-validating reader accept |
| source text passed through (graphml) | 7 | deviation | an attr.type the source declared and GraphML does not define is written back as declared (the importer kept it as text with W_UNKNOWN_ATTR_TYPE); the source was already schema-invalid |
| source date passed through (gexf) | 2 | deviation | a meta lastmodifieddate the source wrote in another date syntax is written back as read; the source was already schema-invalid |
| GEXF infinite weight spelling (gexf) | 96 | known failure | an infinite edge weight is written `Infinity`; the XSD types weight xs:float, whose spelling is INF / -INF (Gephi's Java parser reads Infinity, not INF, so the fix needs a decision) |
| GraphML attr.name outside NMTOKEN (graphml) | 5 | known failure | a column name is written as attr.name unchecked; a name with a space, or the `<name>#<id>` of graph-io's own rename rule, is not an NMTOKEN |
| GEXF 1.3 date attribute type (gexf) | 4 | known failure | a date / dateTime column is declared with type="date" / "dateTime"; GEXF 1.3's attrtype-type has no such types (they are timeformat values), so the column should be written as string or its time value |
| JGF numeric edge id (jgf) | 2 | known failure | a numeric edge id is written as a JSON number; the JGF v2 schema requires a string |
